what: Critical architectural tradeoff: you can have any 3 of {closed-source protection, local-first privacy, free distribution tier, hard revenue gating} but not all 4. Claude Code picked semi-open + server + free trial + API-key gating. Aide-memory currently wants closed + local + free + gated which is impossible. Must pick 3. Options: (A) Accept local-first reality — semi-open client, free is the distribution engine, compete on convenience/updates/support not hard locks. (B) Add a server for "intelligent" features (config gen, cleanup, team sync) — gives real gating but breaks local-first privacy. The "valuable" parts of aide-memory are algorithms which are easy to replicate once understood, so binary protection gives limited value without server-side logic.
why: Fundamental architecture vs business model constraint. This is the blocker for finalizing the product strategy. Every successful dev tool SaaS (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Vercel, Supabase) uses client-open + server-controlled pattern. Aide-memory's local-first stance creates an unresolvable tension with hard revenue gating.
